title: Does inbreeding lead to decreased human fertility?
screen_note: Consanguinity raises fetal loss; asks whether completed fertility falls as a result. Directly the accounting-identity-versus-net-effect question, and a companion to the Ober Hutterite anchor.

title: Natality Decline and Miscarriages Associated With the 1918 Influenza Pandemic: The Scandinavian and United States Experiences
screen_note: Bloom-Feshbach: 1918 pandemic -> natality decline attributed to miscarriage, monthly birth series 1911-1930 for the US and three Scandinavian countries. Anchor-quality; the chapter's best non-famine shock design.

title: Civil conflict, gender-specific fetal loss, and selection: A new test of the Trivers–Willard hypothesis
screen_note: Journal of Health Economics: civil conflict and gender-specific fetal loss, framed as a selection test. An economics-grade identification strategy on exactly B.5's channel; no abstract in the index, so retrieval is a priority.

title: Non-visualized pregnancy losses are prognostically important for unexplained recurrent miscarriage
screen_note: Prior non-visualised losses and the chance of live birth in a subsequent pregnancy.

title: Chance of live birth: a nationwide, registry-based cohort study
screen_note: Registry study of how the sequence of prior losses and births predicts the chance of a live birth in the NEXT pregnancy -- the attenuation parameter measured directly.

title: Chernobyl fallout and outcome of pregnancy in Finland.
screen_note: Chernobyl fallout by Finnish municipality, with live births, stillbirths, pregnancy loss AND induced abortion as outcomes. An exogenous exposure shock with the full outcome set, so the induced/spontaneous separation of Wall 4 is testable here.

title: The Effects of Food Shortage on Human Reproduction
screen_note: Food shortage and human reproduction: the post-war Dresden fertility decline attributed to a food-supply collapse, with concurrent epidemics of miscarriage and low birthweight. A famine shock with a BIRTHS outcome and the loss channel named.

title: Fertility after recurrent miscarriages: results of an observational cohort study
screen_note: Fertility after recurrent miscarriage, 719 couples; subsequent reproductive outcome given a loss history.

title: Trying to Conceive After an Early Pregnancy Loss
screen_note: Time to pregnancy and live birth by the interval between an early loss and resuming attempts, from the EAGeR trial. The recovery-time parameter measured directly, which is what converts an accounting share into a net effect.

title: Fertility Decline and the 1918 Influenza Pandemic in Taiwan
screen_note: Taiwan 1906-1943 monthly death and birth series, cross-correlating pandemic excess deaths with the subsequent birth deficit. A second setting for the 1918 shock design.

title: Fertility Fluctuations in Times of War and Pandemic Influenza
screen_note: Correspondence disputing whether the 1919-20 natality decline was influenza-induced miscarriage rather than wartime behaviour. The identification debate inside the chapter's key shock, so it is read with the paper it contests.

title: A crisis in the life course? Pregnancy loss impacts fertility desires and intentions
screen_note: Advances in Life Course Research: whether experiencing a pregnancy loss changes subsequent fertility DESIRES AND INTENTIONS. A stated-intention outcome, so it pools only with other stated-intention estimates, and it is the behavioural half of the replacement question.

title: Long-term health outcomes from inbreeding in a historical Swedish population: longevity, fertility, and impairments
screen_note: Historical Swedish population: inbreeding against longevity, FERTILITY and impairments, exploiting the 1844 legalisation of consanguineous marriage. Fertility is the outcome and elevated fetal loss is the presumed channel, so the channel needs confirming at full text -- but the design and period are the chapter's.

title: Stillbirth Risk during the 1918 Influenza Pandemic in Arizona, USA
screen_note: Stillbirth risk during the 1918 pandemic, 21,334 Maricopa County birth records. Individual-level records for the shock the aggregate series only infers.

title: Fertility dynamics through historical pandemics and COVID-19 in Switzerland, 1871–2022
screen_note: Population Studies: Swiss general fertility rates 1871-2022 across the 1889-90, 1918-20, 1957 and COVID pandemics, with births falling six to nine months after each peak and MISCARRIAGE offered as the explanation. A repeated shock in one long series, and the closest thing the chapter has to a replication design.

title: Fertility, time to pregnancy, and pregnancy outcomes among women with recurrent miscarriages in the UK: a prospective observational longitudinal study
screen_note: Prospective longitudinal fertility, time-to-pregnancy and outcomes after recurrent miscarriage. Measures the recovery process the net-effect calculation needs.

title: Intra-Uterine Mortality in Morocco: Measures and Impact on Fertility
venue: Journal of Population and Social Studies
screen_note: Morocco: constructs an intrauterine-mortality life table with early and late fetal components AND estimates its effect on women's fertility. Exactly the chapter's primary estimand, in a mid-transition setting. Obscure venue; retrieval and quality check are priorities.

title: The impact of early pregnancy complications on completed family size—A nationwide, registry‐based cohort study with 40 years of data
screen_note: Danish national registry, 458,475 women born 1957-72 followed age 20-45, outcome COMPLETED FAMILY SIZE. The strongest primary-cell record found: a BEHAVIORAL_NET estimand in a controlled-fertility population, which is precisely where the scope doc predicts the effect should vanish.

title: Hypersecretion of luteinising hormone, infertility, and miscarriage
screen_note: LH hypersecretion spanning infertility and miscarriage; no abstract, margins not separated.

title: The pathogenesis of infertility and early pregnancy loss in polycystic ovary syndrome
venue: Best Practice & Research Clinical Obstetrics & Gynaecology
screen_note: PCOS pathogenesis spanning infertility and early loss; no abstract, margins not separated.

title: Infertility and early pregnancy loss
venue: American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynecology
screen_note: No abstract. Title spans both the conception and survival margins (Wall 2) with nothing to decompose them on.

title: Adverse pregnancy outcomes, ‘stillbirths and early neonatal deaths’ in Mutare district, Zimbabwe (2014): a descriptive study
screen_note: Zimbabwe: stillbirths and early neonatal deaths reported as one perinatal category.

title: TIME TRENDS AND DETERMINANTS OF COMPLETED FAMILY SIZE IN A RURAL COMMUNITY FROM THE BASQUE AREA OF SPAIN (1800–1969)
screen_note: Completed family size in a rural Basque community 1800-1969, across the demographic transition. Completed fertility over the FDT is exactly the chapter's outcome and period, but the abstract does not say whether fetal loss enters the analysis. Retrieve before routing.

title: Perinatal Mortality and its Causes in a Rural Block in Tamil Nadu, Southern India: A Community-Based Nonconcurrent Cohort Study
screen_note: Perinatal mortality, Tamil Nadu; stillbirth and early neonatal components combined.

title: Infertility and subsequent recurrent miscarriage: Current state of the literature and future considerations for practice and research
screen_note: Infertility alongside recurrent miscarriage; the conception and survival margins are the subject and are not separated (Wall 2).

title: [Perinatal mortality in Brazil in 2018: an epidemiological analysis according to the modified Wigglesworth classification].
screen_note: Brazilian perinatal mortality under the modified Wigglesworth classification; fetal and early neonatal combined.

title: A retrospective analysis of the risk factors leading to perinatal mortality at a tertiary care hospital of Sikkim, India
venue: International Journal of Reproduction Contraception Obstetrics and Gynecology
screen_note: Perinatal mortality risk factors, Sikkim; stillbirth and neonatal components not separated.

title: Predictors of perinatal mortality in the seven major hospitals of Lusaka Zambia: A case control study
screen_note: Perinatal mortality predictors, Lusaka; components combined.

title: Determinants Of Perinatal Mortality In Bahir Dar Town Governmental Health Institutions, Northwest, Ethiopia, 2019: Prospective Unmatched Case Control Study
screen_note: Perinatal mortality case-control, Bahir Dar; preprint.

title: Magnitude of perinatal mortality in sub-Saharan Africa since 2000: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol
screen_note: Perinatal mortality meta-analysis protocol, sub-Saharan Africa.

title: It's Raining Babies? Flood Exposures and Fertility in Bangladesh
screen_note: PDR: flood exposure and fertility in Bangladesh. A shock with a fertility outcome, but the abstract does not say whether the channel is fetal loss or behaviour. Wall-2-type ambiguity; defer rather than guess.
